pairs.question: Utrum intellectus daemonis sit obtenebratus per privationem cognitionis omnis veritatis?
pairs.answer: Harum autem trium cognitionum prima in daemonibus nec est ablata, nec est diminuta.
pairs.derivation: The article's disputed question (Utrum...) is the genuine interrogative; the author answers it in the Respondeo. Dropped the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod' and the opening division sentence ('duplex est cognitio veritatis...') which sets up categories rather than answering whether ALL truth-knowledge is removed. Took the operative answering sentence stating the first (natural) cognition is neither removed nor diminished; stopped at its full stop, before the further elaboration on the second and third cognitions ('Consequitur enim ipsam naturam angeli...').

pairs.question: Utrum voluntas daemonum sit obstinata in malo?
pairs.answer: Tenendum est firmiter, secundum fidem catholicam, quod et voluntas bonorum angelorum confirmata est in bono, et voluntas daemonum obstinata est in malo.
pairs.derivation: Article-level disputed question answered by the author. Skipped the non-answering preamble of the Respondeo, which reports and refutes Origen's position ('Respondeo dicendum quod Origenis positio fuit... est tanquam erronea reputanda'); advanced the answer start to the operative determinative clause 'Unde haec positio...'—trimmed the connective 'Unde haec positio est tanquam erronea reputanda et' so the answer begins at 'tenendum est firmiter', normalizing capitalization. Stopped at the full stop before 'Causam autem huius obstinationis oportet accipere...' which begins the explanatory elaboration.

pairs.question: Utrum dolor sit in daemonibus?
pairs.answer: Et necesse est dicere quod in eis sit dolor.
pairs.derivation: Article-level disputed question answered by the author. Skipped the opening distinction of the Respondeo ('Respondeo dicendum quod timor, dolor, gaudium... sic possunt esse in daemonibus'), which sets up the passion/act-of-will distinction rather than answering. Took the operative answering sentence affirming that pain is in them; stopped at its full stop, before the justification 'Quia dolor, secundum quod significat...'.

pairs.question: Utrum aer iste sit locus poenalis daemonum?
pairs.answer: Sic ergo daemonibus duplex locus poenalis debetur.
pairs.derivation: Article-level disputed question answered by the author. Skipped the long non-answering preamble of the Respondeo about angels' mediating nature and divine providence ('Respondeo dicendum quod angeli, secundum suam naturam... per malos angelos fieri...'); advanced to the concluding operative sentence introducing the two penal places. Stopped at its full stop; the immediately following sentences ('Unus quidem ratione suae culpae: et hic est infernus. Alius autem ratione exercitationis humanae: et sic debetur eis caliginosus aer.') specify that the dark air is indeed one of them but are elaboration past the first full stop of the answering conclusion.
